entities.name: GlmU
observations: Exact sequence match to reviewed Haemophilus influenzae GlmU reference Q4QMS5; length 456 aa and 100% coverage.

Bifunctional enzyme with N-terminal UDP-N-acetylglucosamine pyrophosphorylase domain (residues 1–229) and C-terminal glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase domain (residues 251–456), separated by a linker.
Catalyzes formation of GlcNAc-1-P from glucosamine-1-P and acetyl-CoA, then UDP-GlcNAc from GlcNAc-1-P and UTP.
Binds one Mg2+ ion per subunit; annotated as a cytosolic homotrimer.
Sequence-derived properties: 456 aa, molecular weight 49,215.66 Da, theoretical pI 6.038, predicted charge at pH 7 −5.52, instability index 18.95, GRAVY −0.104.

Pfam evidence supports an N-terminal nucleotide-transferase region and C-terminal acetyltransferase/hexapeptide-repeat region; domains include NTP_transferase, NTP_transf_3, GMPPB_C, Hexapep and Hexapep_2.
Annotated EC activities are 2.7.7.23 and 2.3.1.157; associated with UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis, peptidoglycan synthesis and lipid A biosynthesis.

entities.name: GlcN-1-P acetylation
observations: Glucosamine-1-phosphate + acetyl-CoA produces N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + CoA; Rhea RHEA:13725.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc formation
observations: N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + UTP produces UDP-N-acetylglucosamine + diphosphate; Rhea RHEA:13509.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU performs the final two enzymatic steps of de novo UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis in bacteria.

entities.name: GlmU sequence properties
observations: Length 456 aa; calculated molecular weight 49.22 kDa; theoretical pI 6.04; GRAVY −0.104; charge at pH 7 approximately −5.52; instability index 18.95.
